name: Petrobras 3W
holds: Labelled sensor recordings of normal operation and nine kinds of anomaly in offshore wells: real, simulated and hand-drawn.
about: Petrobras publishes 3W to train and test detectors of undesirable events in offshore oil wells. PetroDB republishes it as four tables. An Instance is one window of sensor readings taken once a second, framed around one Event class: normal operation or one of nine kinds of anomaly. Each Instance is one Observations file, and the Instance catalog describes every one of them without opening it.

Well kind says where an Instance comes from: a real well (anonymised by Petrobras), a simulator, or a series drawn by hand. Each Observation carries a class label: normal, the anomaly's transient phase (its Event class + 100), or its steady state. Sensor columns keep their upstream names, hyphens included, so quote them in SQL: "P-TPT". The schema document describes each one.

units.unit: valve state: 0 closed, 0.5 partly open, 1 open

queries.title: Find Instances in the catalog
queries.why: The Instance catalog is one 100 kB file with a row per Instance. Pick Instances here by Event class, Well kind or length; source_url is the address of each one's Observations file.
queries.sql:
SELECT instance_id, well_id, start_ts,
       round(duration_s / 3600, 1) AS hours,
       n_rows, source_url
FROM '{base}/petrobras_3w/instances.parquet'
WHERE event_class = 8          -- Hydrate in Production Line
  AND well_kind = 'real'
ORDER BY start_ts;
queries.polars:
import polars as pl

instances = (
    pl.scan_parquet("{base}/petrobras_3w/instances.parquet")
    .filter((pl.col("event_class") == 8) & (pl.col("well_kind") == "real"))   # Hydrate in Production Line
    .select(
        "instance_id", "well_id", "start_ts",
        (pl.col("duration_s") / 3600).round(1).alias("hours"),
        "n_rows", "source_url",
    )
    .sort("start_ts")
    .collect()
)

queries.title: Every real-well Observation of one Event class
queries.why: The Observations are split into one file per Instance, in a folder per Event class. Read the file list first and keep one folder, then query those files together.
queries.sql:
SET VARIABLE observations = (
    SELECT list('{base}/petrobras_3w/observations/' || path)
    FROM read_json('{base}/petrobras_3w/observations/_files.json') AS manifest(path)
    WHERE path LIKE 'event_class=8/%'   -- Hydrate in Production Line
);

SELECT instance_id, class,
       count(*) AS observations,
       avg("P-TPT") / 1e5 AS p_tpt_bar   -- sensors report pascals
FROM read_parquet(getvariable('observations'), hive_partitioning = true)
WHERE well_kind = 'real'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY instance_id, class;
queries.python:
import json, urllib.request
import duckdb

base = "{base}/petrobras_3w/observations/"
files = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "_files.json"))
urls = [base + path for path in files if path.startswith("event_class=8/")]   # Hydrate in Production Line

hydrate = duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT instance_id, class,
           count(*) AS observations,
           avg("P-TPT") / 1e5 AS p_tpt_bar   -- sensors report pascals
    FROM read_parquet($urls, hive_partitioning = true)
    WHERE well_kind = 'real'
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY instance_id, class
""", params={"urls": urls}).df()
queries.polars:
import json, urllib.request
import polars as pl

base = "{base}/petrobras_3w/observations/"
files = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "_files.json"))
urls = [base + path for path in files if path.startswith("event_class=8/")]   # Hydrate in Production Line

hydrate = (
    pl.scan_parquet(urls, hive_partitioning=True)
    .filter(pl.col("well_kind") == "real")
    .group_by("instance_id", "class")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("observations"),
        (pl.col("P-TPT").mean() / 1e5).alias("p_tpt_bar"),   # sensors report pascals
    )
    .sort("instance_id", "class")
    .collect()
)

source.text: Data from 3W, published by Petrobras on GitHub. PetroDB keeps the sensor values and labels as they are and adds the catalog tables.
